subject: art-and-design
topicName: Formal Elements Line Colour Tone Shape Form Texture Pattern

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Line: defines edges, creates movement, suggests direction. Colour: communicates emotion, creates emphasis, establishes mood. Tone: creates form, depth and atmosphere through light and dark.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Shape (2D) and form (3D): geometric shapes feel man-made; organic shapes feel natural. Texture: actual (real surface) vs visual (implied through mark-making).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Pattern: the repetition of a motif — can be regular (predictable) or irregular (organic, varied).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Formal elements are the BUILDING BLOCKS of visual language — understanding them gives you the vocabulary to analyse and create effectively.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
